## Task: FieldError when migrating a field to a new model subclass (django-12754-panel, Django 3.2)

**Root cause.** In `django/db/migrations/autodetector.py`, `generate_created_models()` adds a dependency on each base model's *existence* (`(app, base, None, True)`), but nothing ties `RemoveField(base.title)` to `CreateModel(Book)`. `_sort_migrations()` therefore keeps insertion order — `CreateModel(Book)` first — and applying it renders `Book` against a `Readable` that still has `title`, raising `FieldError: Local field 'title' in class 'Book' clashes with field of the same name from base class 'Readable'`. Reversing the operations by hand works, exactly as the ticket says.

**Fix (18 lines added, source only, no test changes, nothing committed).** In `generate_created_models()`, alongside the existing base-existence dependency, the new model now also depends on the *removal* of any base field it re-declares (a field being moved down to the subclass): for each dotted base in `model_state.bases`, if a base field name also appears in `model_state.fields` and is in `old_field_keys - new_field_keys`, a `(base_app, base, field, False)` dependency is added. `check_dependency()` already maps that tuple to `RemoveField`, and `_sort_migrations()`'s stable topological sort then places the `RemoveField` first. The `removed_field_keys` set is computed once per call, outside the model loop.
